readout_other: Local field potentials recorded epidurally/intracortically and, in the transcranial series, non-invasively from the skull/scalp with an EEG-style electrode
direction_notes: FUS directly evoked short-latency presynaptic (Spike 1) and postsynaptic (Spike 2/3) spikes and excitatory waves W1 and W2 in barrel cortex; these excitatory responses were in turn modulated by fast (GABA_A-like) inhibition acting on Spikes 2/3 and W1, and slow (GABA_B-like) inhibition acting on W2, demonstrated via burst-repetition suppression.
safety_notes: Pressures/mechanical indices (MI up to 1.9) and Ispta values were kept within FDA diagnostic-ultrasound safety limits (e.g. Ispta ~2% of the 720 mW/cm2 FDA limit); no explicit adverse-event monitoring was reported for this acute, nonsurvival animal study.

target.label: barrel column receiving projection from whisker C2 (barrel cortex)

timing.protocol_description: Most experiments used a single continuous 4 MHz tone burst of 50 microseconds duration delivered via the exposed dura (or transcranially through skull/scalp), repeated across ~100-200 epochs (roughly every 1.6-2 s) for signal averaging; in one experiment burst duration was varied from 5 to 1000 microseconds to test temporal precision. In a separate paired-burst paradigm, trains of four 50-microsecond bursts were presented with inter-burst intervals of 10-500 ms to probe fast and slow cortical inhibition. Derated peak negative pressure up to 3.84 MPa (MI=1.9) was used.

exposures.label: 2.2 MHz (also called 2.1 MHz) FUS to barrel cortex (dura/skull/scalp)

target.label: barrel column receiving projection from whisker C2 (barrel cortex)

timing.protocol_description: The in-house conical 2.2 MHz transducer (same as used previously in vitro) was applied to the same barrel-cortex target via dura, skull or scalp using a pressure of 1.2 MPa (MI=0.81); focal FWHM was 1.1 mm transverse by 5.0 mm longitudinal.

source_quotes.n_subjects: There were 42 rats in this entire study: 9 rats showing the strong W2 response (Fig. 1), 6 rats showing activation of a slow inhibitory system for W2 (Fig. 2), 5 rats showing activation of a fast inhibitory system for Spike 2, 3 and W1 (Fig. 3), 3 rats in the TTX experiment (Fig. 4), 4 rats in the Kyna experiment (Fig. 4), 5 rats in the study of the laminar depth profile of the LFP (Fig. 5), 7 rats for the study of duration effects (Fig. 6), and 5 rats for the study of pressure effect and 3 rats for the transcranial study.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In most of the first series of experiments, the barrel column receiving projection from whisker C2 was stimulated with a focal beam of 4 MHz
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: The maximum PNP used in this study was 3.84 MPa, with MI = 1.9.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The duration was varied between for 5 μs and 1000 μs in one experiment.
source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: We also used an in-house 2.2 MHz transducer since FUS penetrates the skull more easily at lower frequencies.
source_quotes.exposures[1].unspecified_domain.pressure: We used a pressure of 1.2 MPa, which has a mechanical index (MI = 0.81) below the safety limit of 1.9.
source_quotes.exposures[1].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: The value of Ispta was $1 . 3 \mathrm { m W / c m ^ { 2 } }$ , again well below the maximum safe energy level.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: For underated PNP = 3.97 MPa, Ispta = 468 W/cm<sup>2</sup>\*duty cycle = 14.6 $\mathrm { { m W / c m ^ { 2 } } } .$
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.ispta_w_cm2: For underated PNP = 3.97 MPa, Ispta = 468 W/cm<sup>2</sup>\*duty cycle = 14.6 $\mathrm { { m W / c m ^ { 2 } } } .$
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: We calculated Ispta as equal to Isptp\*duty cycle (Cullion et al., 2018), where Isptp $( = \Delta \mathrm { P } ^ { 2 } / ( 2 \rho \mathrm { c } ) , \Delta \mathrm { P } =$ peak negative pressure PNP of the FUS burst in Pascal, ρ = material density (1080 ${ \dot { \bf k } } { \bf g } / { \bf m } ^ { 3 }$ for brain), c = propagation velocity of ultrasound in brain (1560 m/s), and duty cycle is 50 μs/1.6 s = 0.003125%).
